Subject: Draft: burst runway calculator + ops checklist for Astra deployment

Hi team and Ashley,

I pulled together a first-pass "runway" calculator for Astra's private VPC deployment and a concise ops checklist for the on-prem networking handoff. The goal here is to move from high-level SLOs to concrete GPU pool sizing assumptions we can commit to for the pilot.

Key questions I want answers to from infra before we share with Astra's infra team:
- What steady-state throughput (tokens/sec) can we commit per G4dn-equivalent pod at 512 token avg seq?
- What warm-pool headroom should we budget for 3x sudden burst for the first 4 weeks?
- Egress constraints: can we support 1.5x observed peak without queueing-induced latency spikes?

I've put a lightweight workbook attached with scenarios (conservative / expected / optimistic) and a simple cost/time-to-warm calculation. Please review the "expected" scenario first — that's what we usually baseline against.

Attachments: runway_calculator_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, scenarios + formulas)

Next steps I propose:
1) Jonas + Rishi: validate kernels and expected per-GPU token throughput numbers and confirm realistic warm-up times.
2) Laura: confirm ops checklist items (DR tests, network ACLs, monitoring hooks) and add any required playbook steps.
3) Me: consolidate and send an Astra-facing runbook by EOD Monday.

If Ashley — thanks for the initial traffic samples. If you can drop the 30-minute traffic histogram (UTC) that would help nail the burst windows.

—Vanessa

Thanks Vanessa — this looks very helpful. Quick clarifications from our side so your assumptions align with ours:

1) Average sequence length: our payloads vary, but the 512 token assumption maps to ~90% of production. Peak bursts are typically shorter (200–300 tokens) but with higher concurrency.
2) Egress: we have an egress bandwidth cap in the EU region but the US VPC will be uncapped. For the pilot we'll place the cluster in our East US colo.
3) Warm pools: we can tolerate ~15s cold-start on a best-effort basis for edge cases, but our UX product team wants <3s 95th for user-facing requests.

I'll attach two items in a follow-up: anonymized 48-hr traffic histogram and our internal SLA excerpt. Also please include Tom from our infra team in subsequent network-level planning.

Thanks,

On Sat, Jun 6, 2026 at 9:12 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Key questions I want answers to from infra before we share with Astra's infra team:
> - What steady-state throughput (tokens/sec) can we commit per G4dn-equivalent pod at 512 token avg seq?

Quick technical reply with my current numbers and assumptions — these are per-GPU measured on our internal benchmark suite (perf v7):
- Baseline (512 tokens avg, FP16 kernel): ~1,800 tokens/sec sustained per A100-sized pod equivalent (G4dn is lower; for G4dn-equivalent estimate ~950 tokens/sec).
- Cold-start token cost: first 2 tokens incur model weight load; warm-up to full inference ramp takes ~8–12s depending on disk cache hit.
- For mixed-ratio traffic (200–512 tokens) use a 0.75 multiplier on baseline throughput.

I attached a tightened calculator (runway_calculator_v2.xlsx) with the microbenchmarks column I took from perf v7. Notes:
- If we assume Astra's UX needs <3s 95th, we need at minimum 30% warm-pool coverage for user-facing routes in week 0, +50% if we want to keep 99th under 3s during 3x burst spikes.
- Network egress: if egress bandwidth is >1Gbps per node we're fine for expected peaks; if it's 100–300Mbps we need to shard requests or increase GPU count.

Action: Rishi — can you validate the disk-cache hit assumptions (we've seen variation across providers) and mark the conservative/expected flags in the sheet?

Attachment: runway_calculator_v2.xlsx (updated with perf v7 columns)

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Infra Performance Lead
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft: burst runway calculator + ops checklist for Astra deployment

Thanks — great context. I pulled together a one-page ops checklist and a simple network topology diagram for the Astra pilot; attaching both. Summary of recommended commitments for the pilot:

Pilot commitments (proposed):
- Baseline throughput commitment: 900 tokens/sec per G4dn-equivalent pod (expected scenario).
- Warm-pool coverage: 35% of user-facing capacity in week 0, ramp to 60% by week 3.
- Surge handling: plan for 3x concurrency spikes with graceful degradation rules:
  - Step 1: Burst admission control (queue max 200ms)
  - Step 2: Route non-critical work to lower-cost dedicated queue (best-effort)
  - Step 3: Autoscale + warm-pool spin-up (target spin-up <12s)
- Observability hooks: token-level latency histogram, per-route error budget, prefix cache hit ratio.

Network checklist highlights:
- Ensure BGP route exchange with Astra colo (ASN info in drawio).
- Reserve 1.5Gbps egress per rack as safeguard for peak windows.
- Firewall/NAT rules: open ports 443 + 10250 (k8s node agent) between Redwood control plane IPs and Astra management VPC.

Attachments: private-deploy-network_topology.drawio, ops_checklist_v1.md

Next steps:
- Rishi: validate disk-cache hit assumptions by EOD Wednesday (call out any provider-specific variance).
- Laura: run through DR checklist and add any compliance hooks Astra needs for pilot (audit logging, retention).
- Ashley/Tom: confirm egress/ASN details and send the traffic histogram link.

If we get all this by Thu EOD we can lock pilot commitments and present a final runbook to Astra Friday.

—Vanessa
